source: NCERT Class VIII, Social and Political Life III, Polity Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. What the Judiciary Does
points: The **judiciary** is the system of **courts** that interprets and applies the law and settles disputes.

sub: **Dispute resolution** — between citizens, citizen and government, or two governments.
**Judicial review** — the power to **strike down laws** that violate the Constitution.
**Upholding fundamental rights** — anyone can approach the courts if their rights are violated.

sections.heading: 2. An Independent Judiciary
points: India has an **independent judiciary** — separated from the **legislature and executive** (separation of powers).
This means the government cannot interfere in judicial decisions; judges decide impartially.
Independence lets the courts protect citizens' rights against the misuse of state power.

sections.heading: 3. Structure of the Courts
points: India has an **integrated (single) system** of courts, in a **pyramid**:

sub: **Supreme Court** — at the top (in New Delhi), headed by the **Chief Justice of India**; its decisions bind all courts.
**Subordinate / District courts** — at the district and local level.

points: Cases can move up on **appeal** from lower to higher courts.

sections.heading: 4. Access to Justice — PIL
points: Justice should be accessible to all, but courts are costly and slow.
**Public Interest Litigation (PIL)** — from the 1980s, **any person or group** can approach the court on behalf of those whose rights are violated (even by a letter/postcard).
PIL has helped the **poor and marginalised** get justice on issues like bonded labour, environment and rights.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Judiciary: dispute resolution + judicial review + upholding fundamental rights.
Independent judiciary = separated from legislature & executive.
Integrated structure: Supreme Court → High Courts → District/subordinate courts.
Supreme Court in New Delhi, headed by the Chief Justice of India; its rulings bind all.
PIL (since the 1980s) lets anyone seek justice for others — helps the marginalised.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: India has an **integrated (single) judiciary** — Supreme Court at the top, binding all courts.
**Judicial review** = courts can **strike down unconstitutional laws**.
An **independent judiciary** is separated from the **executive and legislature**.
**PIL** allows a **third party** to seek justice for those who cannot themselves approach the court.
